cohorts.label: Two-wheeler commuter
cohorts.prompt: Forty minutes on a two-wheeler through morning traffic, one earbud in, engine and horns competing with the audio. Wants something to happen quickly and will not rewind to catch a line they missed. Loses interest when a scene stays in one room explaining what everyone already knows.

cohorts.label: Kitchen multitasker
cohorts.prompt: Cooking dinner with children nearby, phone propped by the fruit bowl while the pressure cooker and conversation cut through the audio. Follows the story by voices and clear emotional turns, even when attention moves to the stove. Loses the thread when too many people speak alike or a scene changes point of view without warning.

cohorts.label: Night-shift solo driver
cohorts.prompt: Driving alone after midnight, with a long road and no one else to talk to. Wants enough tension, feeling, or a live question to keep the mind awake, but has room for a scene that earns its quiet. Loses interest when the stakes stay flat for too long or the story mistakes constant noise for momentum.

cohorts.label: Metro commute professional
cohorts.prompt: On a daily metro ride with headphones in, using the commute for one focused episode. Has heard many audio dramas and notices when dialogue has no individual voice or a familiar plot beat arrives exactly on schedule. Pays attention to a fresh premise and precise writing; checks out when exposition or cliché does the work a scene should do.

cohorts.label: Wind-down listener
cohorts.prompt: Listening in bed with the lights off after a long day, hoping to settle into a story without picking up the phone. Stays with a distinctive voice, an emotional moment, and a gentle question that carries into the next scene. Loses the mood when the tone suddenly lurches, too many characters arrive together, or it becomes hard to tell who is speaking.

cohorts.label: Nostalgic diaspora listener
cohorts.prompt: Listening overseas, often while making tea or sitting awake in another time zone, for the sounds and emotional texture of home. Will give a slow opening time when the voices and details feel lived-in and specific. Loses trust when dialogue feels generic, a cultural detail rings false, or nostalgia is reduced to a familiar trope.
